entries.summary: Block 9 Audio Engine wired to real commands: AUDIO DEVICES/START/STOP/ON/OFF/STATUS/GAIN -- previously dead code with zero command or GUI surface
details: Re-audited the full established roadmap first (GUI polish, manual popup, changelog popup, MIDI-held FLASH, Block 12 AI layer, MIDI mapping GUI, attribute pool panels) -- all confirmed already landed by prior sessions, by reading the actual code, not just trusting the changelog. Went looking for the next real gap instead of re-doing finished work, per this session's own instructions.

Found one: AudioEngine and AudioMapper (Block 9) were fully built -- real-time RMS + 3-band FFT capture, attack/release envelope smoothing, and a threaded mapper that writes bass=red/mid=green/high=blue/level=dim into output_state.audio_layer, which the OutputState merge pipeline already blends in above cue/executor layers -- but neither class was ever instantiated at module level, and there was no command verb or GUI control to reach them at all. A prior session's own comment at the AudioEngine import guard explicitly flagged this ('AudioEngine/AudioMapper are not wired into any command handler or GUI panel yet').

Instantiated audio_engine and audio_mapper at module level alongside midi/osc. Capture is opt-in (AUDIO START), unlike MIDI/OSC which the console brings up automatically -- a microphone is a sensor a user should explicitly choose to turn on, not something that should start listening the moment the console launches. Construction alone (no AUDIO START) touches no hardware and is safe with sounddevice/PortAudio absent, same defensive pattern as the existing MIDI backend-unavailable handling.

New command family in run_command(): AUDIO DEVICES (list input devices), AUDIO START [device index] / AUDIO STOP (capture), AUDIO ON / AUDIO OFF (the reactive mapping layer, independent of capture so a mic can stay running while the layer is toggled for cue timing), AUDIO STATUS (capture/mapping state + current band levels), AUDIO GAIN <n> (input sensitivity). All documented in the command manual ('?' popup) under a new AUDIO REACTIVE section.

No GUI panel added this session -- deliberately kept to command-line surface only, since a prior session's changelog entry flagged the main window's vertical layout as already tight for 1920x1080 with the current row count, and this is scoped as backend wiring, not another panel. A GUI meter/toggle for this is a reasonable next step but is a layout decision worth its own pass rather than bolting on here.

Smoke test extended: AUDIO ON/OFF/STATUS/GAIN exercised through the real run_command() dispatcher (not just calling the classes directly), plus AUDIO DEVICES/START exercised in the existing forced-_AUDIO_AVAILABLE=False branch to verify clean error strings with no exception and without opening a real mic stream. audio_mapper.stop() and audio_engine.stop() added to both shutdown paths (headless-exit and normal GUI-exit) so the mapper's background thread is joined on exit like the other engines.

No schema or persisted-data changes -- nothing new to save/load, fully backward compatible. Verified with python3 -m py_compile and STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 (50/50, 43 previous + 7 new); confirmed via git status that studio_data/*.json was untouched by the run. This session's container was also missing the full optional dependency stack (sacn, mido, dearpygui, anthropic, sounddevice, python-osc, numpy, libportaudio2) -- installed to actually exercise AudioEngine with _AUDIO_AVAILABLE=True as well as the forced-False branch, rather than only ever testing the guard path.

entries.summary: Fixed a real bug: OSC grandmaster fader input (/gma3/fader/PAGE/EXEC) never matched its own dispatcher pattern -- dead since the day it was added
details: Roadmap re-audit found nothing new (every item -- GUI polish, manual/glossary popup, changelog popup, executor FLASH-to-MIDI, Block 12 AI layer, MIDI mapping GUI, attribute pool panels -- already landed in prior sessions), so did a deep read of Block 11 (OSC Engine), which had never gotten a dedicated audit the way Blocks 7/9/12 did.

OSCEngine's own docstring and _osc_fader's docstring both document /gma3/fader/PAGE/EXEC as a 2-segment address (e.g. /gma3/fader/1/1), and _osc_fader's own address-parsing code (parts[2]=page, parts[3]=exec) matches that 4-token address. But the registration line read osc.map("/gma3/fader/*/*/*", _osc_fader) -- three wildcard segments, i.e. a 5-token pattern. OSC address-pattern matching (per the pythonosc dispatcher, which implements the OSC spec's segment-count-must-match rule) requires the same number of '/'-separated tokens on both sides; a 5-token pattern cannot match a 4-token address. Verified directly with pythonosc's own Dispatcher.call_handlers_for_packet(): a real /gma3/fader/1/1 message fell through to the default/unmapped handler and never reached _osc_fader, while /gma3/key/1/1/go (whose pattern correctly has 3 wildcards for a 3-segment PAGE/EXEC/TYPE address) matched fine -- confirming the fader line was the only one wrong, not a systemic pattern-matching problem.

Checked git blame/log: this line has only ever been touched once, in the commit that introduced it -- so any MA3-style tool (Chataigne, TouchOSC, Bome) sending a fader move to Studio Console on port 8001 has never once been able to move the grandmaster dim via OSC, silently logged only as '(unmapped)' the whole time.

Fixed by dropping the extra wildcard segment: osc.map("/gma3/fader/*/*", _osc_fader). Verified the fix the same way the bug was found -- feeding a real built OSC packet through the actual dispatcher, not just calling the handler function directly.

Added a new smoke-test check that builds a real /gma3/fader/1/1 OSC packet with pythonosc's OscMessageBuilder and runs it through osc._dispatch.call_handlers_for_packet(), asserting the grandmaster dim (_fader_dim[0]) actually changes -- so a future regression in this pattern is caught by the automated suite instead of requiring another manual dispatcher trace.

One-line functional fix (plus one doc-comment tweak) + one new smoke-test check. No schema or persisted-data changes, fully backward compatible. Verified with python3 -m py_compile and STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 (43/43, 42 previous + 1 new); confirmed via git status that studio_data/*.json was untouched by the run.

entries.summary: First real pixel-verified GUI pass: fixed a Linux/non-Mac font bug hiding half the UI's punctuation, plus one genuine clipping bug
details: Every prior session's changelog entry that touched GUI layout flagged the same limitation: no display access, so sizing/clipping fixes were verified by code review only ('worth a visual check next time the console runs on a real screen', 'no pixel-level layout verification (can't screenshot)'). This session's container has Xvfb *and* working GL software rendering (LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1) plus dearpygui 2.3.1 installable, so — on a throwaway copy of the script + a throwaway copy of studio_data in scratch space, never the real files — built a small harness that calls gui.build(), renders a handful of frames, and dumps dpg.output_frame_buffer() to PNGs, including one per popup by calling each popup's own toggle callback before capturing. This is the first session able to actually look at the rendered console instead of reasoning about widget code.

Main window screenshot at 1920x1080: fits cleanly with room to spare, no scrollbar needed — the GUI-polish roadmap item other sessions could only verify by code review is now confirmed by an actual screenshot.

Found a real, previously invisible bug: _load_console_font() only ever tried to load '/System/Library/Fonts/SFNSMono.ttf' (macOS-only) and silently returned None everywhere else, falling back to DearPyGui's built-in bitmap font. That bitmap font has no glyphs for em/en dash, curly quotes, ellipsis, bullet, or the ▲▼◀▶■□●○ symbols used throughout the UI for status indicators and combo arrows — every one of them rendered as a literal '?'. Visible everywhere once screenshotted: the changelog popup, the command manual, the BACK/GO button glyphs, the 'sel:' status text, MIDI mapping row icons, all of it.

Fixed by trying a short list of common monospace font paths per OS (SF Mono on macOS unchanged; DejaVu Sans Mono and Liberation Mono on Debian/Ubuntu and Fedora/RHEL; Consolas on Windows) and using whichever one actually exists on disk. Also removed the now-pointless add_font_range_hint/add_font_range calls from the old code — confirmed via DeprecationWarning that both are no-ops in dearpygui 2.3.1 ('character ranges are now automatic'), so a loaded font gets full glyph coverage for free; keeping them just printed warnings on every startup for nothing. Re-screenshotted the changelog, manual, MIDI, attribute-pool, executor-pages, patch, FX editor, monitors, color-picker, and AI-prompts popups after the fix — all render real dashes/quotes/arrows/shapes instead of '?' now.

Also found, via the same screenshot pass, a genuine sizing bug the roadmap explicitly calls out: the AI prompts popup (ai_prompts_window) was declared height=480 but its actual content (prompt grid + separator + label + multiline input + save-prompt button) needs more — the 'save prompt' button was rendered partially below the window's own bottom border. Bumped to height=520; re-screenshotted to confirm the button now sits fully inside the window with normal padding.

Backward compatible: on macOS with SF Mono present, behavior is unchanged (same font file, same size). On any OS with none of the candidate font files present, falls back to the exact same None/bitmap-font behavior as before — no new failure mode. No data-model or schema changes; studio_data/*.json untouched (verified: all GUI testing happened against a scratch copy in /tmp, never the real files, and git status after this session's edits shows only studio_project.py + this changelog entry touched). Verified with python3 -m py_compile and STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 (42/42, unchanged from baseline — this was a GUI-only fix the headless smoke test can't itself exercise, hence the separate Xvfb+screenshot verification described above).

entries.summary: Hardened Block 9 (Audio Engine) startup: missing sounddevice/PortAudio no longer crashes the entire console
details: Roadmap re-audit found nothing new (all 7 items already landed across prior sessions), so did a deep read of the one Block that had never gotten a dedicated audit: Block 9, Audio Engine (AudioEngine + AudioMapper). Grepped the whole file for AudioEngine/AudioMapper/audio_engine/audio_mapper usage outside Block 9 itself and found zero hits -- unlike every other Block, this one is fully implemented (RMS level + 3-band FFT analysis, attack/release envelope, a bass=red/mid=green/high=blue/level=dim mapper) but never instantiated, never given a command handler, never surfaced in the GUI, and not mentioned as a roadmap item. It is currently 100% dead code.

Found a real bug while confirming that:  at module level binds to the native PortAudio library at import time (unlike mido/rtmidi, which import lazily and only fail when a port is actually opened -- already hardened in Block 10). On a box without PortAudio installed, this raised a bare OSError and crashed the whole console before a single fixture patched, before the network/MIDI/OSC engines started, before the GUI could even build -- for a feature nothing else in the file uses. Reproduced directly: a fresh environment with sounddevice's Python package but no libportaudio2 failed with 'OSError: PortAudio library not found' at line 3183, killing the entire process.

Fixed by wrapping the sounddevice/numpy imports (numpy is also only used inside this Block) in a try/except that sets _AUDIO_AVAILABLE=False and stashes the error instead of propagating it. AudioEngine.list_devices() now prints a clear 'Audio engine unavailable (...)' message instead of raising when the backend is missing; AudioEngine.start() raises a clean RuntimeError with the underlying cause instead of an opaque OSError/ImportError. This mirrors the existing Block 10 pattern ('MIDI startup hardened against missing MIDI backend entirely').

Verified two ways: (1) simulated a genuinely missing sounddevice package via a sys.meta_path import blocker and confirmed the full STUDIO_DRY_RUN/STUDIO_HEADLESS smoke test now boots and passes end-to-end instead of crashing at import. (2) Added 2 new smoke-test checks that force _AUDIO_AVAILABLE=False directly (restored in a finally block) and assert list_devices() doesn't raise and start() raises RuntimeError specifically -- so this regression is caught automatically on every future run regardless of whether the CI/dev box happens to have a working audio stack installed, not just when someone thinks to test the missing-dependency case by hand.

NEEDS ALIGNMENT (not fixing without direction, flagging for the user like the attribute-pools entry did): AudioEngine/AudioMapper are fully built but entirely unwired -- no AUDIO ON/OFF command, no GUI toggle or level meters, no persistence of the audio-reactive mapping in show files. Options: (a) wire it up as a real feature (needs a command handler, a GUI panel with device picker + live level bars, and a decision on whether the bass/mid/high/level -> RGB/dim mapping should be user-configurable or stay hardcoded), (b) leave as dormant/optional code now that it can no longer crash startup, or (c) remove it entirely if audio-reactive lighting isn't wanted for this rig. This session only fixed the startup-crash bug and did not make a product decision to build out or remove the feature.

No schema or persisted-data changes -- pure import-time robustness fix, fully backward compatible with existing shows. Verified with python3 -m py_compile and STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 (42/42 smoke test, 40 previous + 2 new).

entries.summary: Fix: idle executors had no reachable FLASH button in the GUI (mouse-only operation was broken)
details: Roadmap item 'Executor FLASH mode wired to actual MIDI press-and-hold' was marked done in prior changelogs, and the MIDI path (note-learn → EXEC <n> FLASH ON/OFF) does work correctly. But the mouse-driven path was broken: _rebuild_playbacks() only ever created a flash_btn_{eid} widget for executors where `ex.is_active and ex.cuestack` was true. Executor.is_active only flips to True inside go()/back()/goto()/reload()/flash_on(), and back to False in stop() (which flash_off() calls). Net effect: an executor that has a cuestack ASSIGNed but has never been GO'd — the normal starting state for something you intend to trigger only via FLASH — had no button to click at all, and flash_off() deletes the button again the instant it's released (is_active goes back to False, next rebuild drops the row). The command-line path (EXEC <n> FLASH ON/OFF) always worked; only the physical/mouse control was unreachable for idle executors.

Fix: _rebuild_playbacks(), _playbacks_state_hash(), and the tick-loop's FLASH hold-detection (poll of is_item_active(flash_btn_{eid})) now all gate on `ex.cuestack` alone, not `ex.is_active and ex.cuestack`. The Playbacks panel now lists every executor that has a cuestack assigned, whether it's currently playing a cue or idle, ordered by fire-order first (most recently active) then remaining idle slots by executor number. Idle rows show '▶ —' for the cue label (cs.current is None until first GO), same as before — only the missing widget was the bug, not the labeling.

active_layers() (the actual DMX output merge) and the AI-context / LIST-command 'active executors' summaries were deliberately left untouched — those correctly mean 'currently contributing to output', which idle-but-assigned executors are not. Only the three GUI-surfacing spots changed.

Verified two ways: (1) STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 smoke test still 40/40. (2) New pixel-level check, not just code review this time — this container has Xvfb, so ran a scratch copy of the repo (own studio_data copy, real show untouched) under xvfb-run with dearpygui.dearpygui.start_dearpygui monkeypatched to run real render frames instead of blocking. Assigned a cuestack to an idle executor via ASSIGN CS 1 TO EXEC 5 (never GO'd), rebuilt the playbacks panel, and confirmed flash_btn_5 now exists as a real widget and executor 5 is included in the tick loop's flash-hold poll set. Before this fix that widget would not have existed.
No schema or persisted-data changes — pure GUI/behavior fix over existing executor state. Backward compatible: no new fields, no changed save format.

entries.summary: Expanded smoke test to cover RECORD GROUP/FORM/FX + attribute pools (all passed); flagging attribute pools (position/gobo/zoom/focus/beam/control) as dead code for this rig — needs a decision
details: Roadmap re-audit found nothing new (all 7 items already landed across prior sessions), so instead of another deep-dive on a single Block, looked for untested-but-implemented command paths the way past sessions found real bugs in Block 7 and Block 12. Found several RECORD paths that had never been exercised by the smoke test: RECORD GROUP (+ GROUP recall), RECORD FORM (custom breakpoint curve) + FORM LIST, and RECORD FX + FIRE FX (roundtrip through the pool and back into the programmer).

Added 12 new smoke-test checks for those paths (2 for GROUP, 2 for FORM, 2 for FX, 6 for the attribute pools below). All passed on first run (one test-authoring mistake caught and fixed along the way: RECORD FORM title-cases its name argument, so a check for the literal string 'SmokeWave' needed to become a case-insensitive match — not a product bug). No new bugs found in GROUP/FORM/FX record/recall — that code is solid.

While adding coverage for the six attribute pools (position/gobo/zoom/focus/beam/control — the GUI popup landed last session), traced why RECORD POSITION etc. always report 'no data in programmer': the patched fixture profile for all 6 units (SGM_RGB_54) only defines red/green/blue channels. There is no command anywhere in the file that writes pan, tilt, gobo, zoom, focus, iris, shutter, strobe, prism, frost, macro, or animation values into the programmer — grepped for 'AT PAN', 'AT GOBO', 'AT ZOOM' etc. and found zero hits. Even if such a command existed, SubFixture.get_dmx_values() only emits channels present in profile.channels, so non-RGB channel data could never reach DMX output for these fixtures regardless.

Net effect: the position/gobo/zoom/focus/beam/control pools and their GUI popup (the 'attr' button) are structurally unable to ever hold real data for this specific rig — 6 SGM LT-200 pixel tubes are static color fixtures with no moving parts, no gobos, no zoom/focus motors. Confirmed this is not a bug in the newly-added smoke test coverage (RECORD gracefully returns a clean 'no data' message rather than crashing, which the new checks now assert), it's a mismatch between a generic moving-light attribute framework built for a future/hypothetical fixture type and the actual patched hardware.

NEEDS ALIGNMENT — not fixing without direction: three options exist and picking one is a product decision, not a bug fix. (a) Leave as-is — harmless dead UI, costs nothing to keep if a moving fixture is ever patched later. (b) Repurpose control_pool specifically for real LT-200 attributes if the real fixture's DMX personality has anything beyond RGB (e.g. a strobe or macro channel) worth exposing — would need the actual LT-200 DMX chart to know what's available and correct to add. (c) Remove the pools/popup entirely as inapplicable to this show's patch. Leaving this for the user rather than guessing which of the three is wanted.
No schema or persisted-data changes. Verification: python3 -m py_compile passes; STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 smoke test passes 40/40 (28 previous + 12 new).

entries.summary: Fixed a real safety bug: BLACKOUT did not cut output for HIGHLIGHTed fixtures
details: Roadmap re-audit again found nothing new (all documented items already landed in prior sessions), so did a deep read of Block 7 (OutputState.get_dmx_for_universe) — the core DMX merge/output path — since it hadn't had a dedicated deep-dive changelog entry the way Block 12 (AI engine) got last session.

Found: the HIGHLIGHT branch in get_dmx_for_universe() set final_r/g/b = 255 unconditionally for highlighted fixtures, completely bypassing the grandmaster fader (gm = self.master_level). Every other output path (the non-highlight else branch) correctly multiplies by gm. Consequence: HIGHLIGHT ON followed by BLACKOUT (which just sets master_level = 0.0) left highlighted fixtures transmitting full white (255,255,255) on the real DMX/sACN line — BLACKOUT is documented and relied on as 'Cut all DMX output instantly', an absolute safety cutoff, and this silently violated that for any fixture still marked highlighted.

Fixed: highlighted fixtures now compute final_r/g/b = int(255 * gm) — full open white *relative to* the grandmaster position, matching how a real desk's highlight function behaves (it can never exceed where the master fader physically sits). Per-fixture dim is still bypassed by design (that's the point of highlight), only the grandmaster relationship was wrong.

Added a smoke-test check: ALL → HIGHLIGHT → BLACKOUT → assert max(dmx) == 0 on the real get_dmx_for_universe() output, not just the flags, so a future regression here is caught the same way it was found.
No schema or persisted-data changes — pure output-computation fix, fully backward compatible with existing shows.
Verification: python3 -m py_compile passes; STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 smoke test passes 28/28 (27 previous + 1 new).

entries.summary: Fixed 4 real bugs in the Block 12 AI engine: frozen cuestack snapshot, wrong stack->executor resolution, dead fade_time action, destructive fx_clear
details: Roadmap re-audit found nothing new (same as every recent session — all 7 items already landed), so did a deep read of Block 12 specifically, since it's the area every prior session's audit checked only at a surface level ('AI actions dispatcher exists and looks complete') rather than tracing each action handler against the rest of the codebase. Found four real bugs, all previously undetected:

(1) AIEngine was constructed with `cuestacks={1: cs1}` — a frozen dict snapshot taken once at startup — instead of a live reference to cuestack_pool. cs2/cs3 exist in cuestack_pool from the same startup block, so the AI was permanently blind to them, and nothing ever updated the snapshot (not LOAD SHOW, not RECORD CS 2, not GUI cuestack creation). Fixed: AIEngine now takes cuestack_pool directly and _state() reads .stacks live, so it always reflects current state including after LOAD SHOW.

(2) Every cue-fire action (goto_cue/cue_go/cue_back/cue_fire) resolved the AI's 'stack' parameter via executor_pool.get(stack_id) — treating a cuestack id as if it were an executor slot id. Since ExecutorPool.get() auto-creates missing slots, this silently fired whatever (possibly wrong, possibly empty) executor happened to share that number, the moment a cuestack was assigned to a differently-numbered executor (e.g. ASSIGN CS 2 TO EXEC 9) — masked until now only by the default 1:1 startup wiring. Any 'Executor N: no cuestack assigned' failure was also discarded, never logged. Fixed: new _exec_for_stack() searches actual executor->cuestack assignments first, falling back to same-numbered slot only if none found; _fire() now logs every fire result including failures.

(3) fade_time set self._last_fade but nothing ever read that field — fully documented in ACTION_SCHEMA, fully inert. The AI could be asked for a slow fade into a cue and would report the action as executed while nothing happened. Fixed: _fire() now consumes a pending fade_time once, applying it as a temporary executor time-override for the very next cue-fire action in the same batch (same restore-after pattern as the existing Executor.flash_on()), then clears it — not a standing default.

(4) fx_clear and fx_stop-with-no-channel called fx_engine.clear() directly. FXEngine.clear() wipes every layer including ones owned by running cue executors (whose ids go stale in ex._fx_ids), and — unlike the real 'FX CLEAR' command handler — never pops the programmer's pending 'fx' defs, so the next programmer-FX rebuild tick could resurrect them. Both actions now route through self._cmd('FX CLEAR'), matching command-line behavior exactly.

Verification: python3 -m py_compile and STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 both pass (27/27, unaffected since the smoke test never sets an API key so this code never runs there). Went further than that this time: built a scratch harness with a fake ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to call ai.execute() directly and check all four fixes against real objects — live stack visibility, correct executor resolution after a cuestack was reassigned away from its default executor, single-use fade_time consumption, and fx_clear actually clearing programmer fx defs. All 6/6 checks passed. That harness also turned up a real but unrelated hazard worth flagging for future sessions: calling ai._log (== gui._log, which calls dpg.set_value on the 'cmd_log' tag) from headless mode segfaults dearpygui's C extension, because gui.build() — which creates that widget — never runs in STUDIO_HEADLESS. Confirmed this is not reachable by real users (the GUI is always built before any AI action can be triggered interactively), so left unfixed, but any future session adding headless-mode coverage of AI logging should route around gui._log or build a stub.
No schema or persisted-data changes — pure internal AIEngine wiring, fully backward compatible with existing shows.

entries.summary: GUI polish: fixed two real popup clipping bugs, found via pixel-level screenshot verification (not just code reading)
details: Roadmap re-audit before touching anything: with the roadmap items all marked done in prior sessions' changelog entries, went looking for a concrete, verifiable bug instead — same pattern the last few sessions used. Confirmed this container has Xvfb + a working dearpygui import under `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1920x1080x24"` (per the technique a prior session documented), so did a full sweep: built the GUI on a scratch copy of the repo under STUDIO_DRY_RUN, opened every popup one at a time via a monkeypatched dpg.start_dearpygui, and captured dpg.output_frame_buffer() screenshots of each — main window plus all 9 floating popups (patch, osc, midi, fx editor, keys/manual, changelog, pages, monitors, color picker).

Main window at 1920x1040 and 8 of the 9 popups rendered cleanly with no clipping. Found two real, previously-undetected sizing bugs in the other two: (1) the color picker popup (_build_color_picker_popup) was fixed at width=310 height=390, but the color wheel widget alone measures 351x313px and the full stack of controls (wheel + R/G/B/hex readout + Apply/White/Off buttons + 8 quick-color swatches + status line) needs ~470px — confirmed via dpg.get_item_pos/get_item_rect_size that the last widget (cpick_status) sits at y=451, past the window's 390px height. In practice this meant the Apply button — the primary way to confirm a picked color — rendered half-cut at the very bottom edge, and all 8 quick-color swatches (Red/Green/Blue/Amber/Cyan/Magenta/Warm/UV) plus the status readout were entirely below the fold with no visible affordance that scrolling would reveal them. (2) The manual/keys popup's command-reference table used plain dpg.add_text with no wrap= for the command-string column, so long command shorthand rows — e.g. '1 AT YELLOW / ORANGE / PINK / PURPLE / LIME / TEAL' — were silently cut off mid-word with no way to read the rest; this affected several of the longer named-colour and LIST rows.

Fixed by (1) resizing color_picker_window to 370x480 — verified via a fresh screenshot that Apply/White/Off and all 8 quick swatches now render fully visible with zero scrolling needed — and (2) adding wrap=280 (cmd column) / wrap=380 (desc column) to the keys-popup table's add_text calls, so long command strings now wrap onto a second line instead of being truncated — verified via a fresh screenshot showing the full 'YELLOW / ORANGE / PINK / PURPLE / LIME / TEAL' string wrapped and readable.

Both are pure sizing/cosmetic tweaks — no schema, data model, or command-handler changes, so no backward-compatibility concerns. Verified with python3 -m py_compile and STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 (27/27 smoke test); confirmed via git status that studio_data/*.json in the real repo was untouched (all screenshot verification ran against a throwaway copy in the scratch dir, never studio_data/popup_layout.json or any other real show file).

This closes out the one remaining open thread on the 'GUI polish: fix any sizing/clipping issues' roadmap item that every prior session had to leave flagged as 'can't verify without a real display' — this session's screenshot sweep covered all 9 popups plus the main window and found these were the only two with real clipping.

entries.summary: Fixed: cue tooltip computed FX layer count but never displayed it (dead variable, wrong key)
details: Roadmap check this session: re-read the full established roadmap (GUI polish, manual popup, changelog popup, executor FLASH-to-MIDI, Block 12 AI layer, MIDI mapping GUI, attribute pool GUI panels) against the current code and changelog history — every item is already implemented by prior sessions (MIDI mapping popup has learn/direct-add/reassign/delete; FLASH is wired to real MIDI note on/off via off_callback; attribute pool panels exist for position/gobo/zoom/focus/beam with right-click Record/Apply/Rename/Clear). No functional gap found there, so this session looked for a concrete bug instead.

Found one via pyflakes ('local variable nfx is assigned to but never used') in the cue-pool tooltip builder (_tick_pools, cue slot loop): `nfx = len(cue.data.get('__fx__', []))` computed a value that was never interpolated into the tooltip string. Worse, the key itself was wrong — grep across the file confirms FX layers are stored per-fixture at `cue.data[fixture_id]['fx']` (see the FX ARCHITECTURE comment near the bottom of the file), never under a top-level '__fx__' key, so `nfx` was always 0 even before the dead-code issue — this line has never worked.

Fixed by summing `len(v.get('fx', []))` over every per-fixture dict entry in cue.data and appending a '\nN FX layer(s)' line to the tooltip (same pattern as the existing fixture-count line), so hovering a cue slot in the pool now actually shows how many FX layers that cue will fire on GO, matching what RECORD CUE already captures.

One-line-scope fix, no schema/data changes, fully backward compatible. Verified with python3 -m py_compile and STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 (8/8 smoke test); confirmed via git status that studio_data/*.json was untouched by the run.

entries.summary: v0.18: pool management improvements — right-click menus, COPY, DELETE, LIST for all pool types
details: Attr pools (position/gobo/zoom/focus/beam/control) now have right-click context menus on every slot button: Record Here, Apply, Rename, Clear. RENAME and CLEAR commands added for all 6 attr pool types.
Rate/size/spread pool buttons in the left column now have right-click menus: Recall, Record Here, Rename, Delete. DELETE RATE/SIZEP/SPREADP commands added.
COPY COLOR/DIM/GROUP/FX N TO M [name] command added — duplicate any pool preset to another slot. Copy option also added to right-click menus on those pool buttons.
LIST POSITION/GOBO/ZOOM/FOCUS/BEAM/CONTROL command added for attr pool inspection.
Stage canvas: each fixture master bar now shows dim% below the fixture name so intensity is visible at a glance without opening the monitors popup.
FX editor slot labels now stay live-refreshed when the editor window is open (so COPY FX and other external changes are immediately visible in the editor).
Cuestack right-click menu: added Assign to Executor option (prefills ASSIGN CS N TO EXEC).
Keys popup (?): documented all new COPY, DELETE RATE/SIZEP/SPREADP, RENAME/CLEAR for attr pools, and LIST for attr pools.
Bug fix: initialized dim=master.virtual_dimmer before the output-engine conditional block in _tick_stage, preventing a NameError when output engine is unavailable.

entries.summary: Fixed: AI bar and header 'ai' button were shown even without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set, permanently busting the 1920x1080 layout budget
details: Real bug, not just documentation: `ai = AIEngine(...)` is always constructed and passed into GUIEngine as `self._ai`, so `if self._ai:` (used to gate both the header 'ai' button and the whole AI prompt bar) was always true — AIEngine has no __bool__/__len__, so a plain instance is always truthy regardless of its self._enabled flag. Every user, not just ones with an API key configured, was getting the AI bar built and the 'ai' header button shown, even though the AI engine internally refuses to do anything (ask() just prints 'set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY first') and the manual popup explicitly documents 'AI bar/buttons are hidden entirely if it isn't set'. Fixed both gates to check `self._ai and self._ai._enabled` instead of bare truthiness.

This also directly serves the 'GUI polish / fit in 1920x1080 with no scrollbars' roadmap item: the layout-budget comment above GUIEngine explicitly carves out the ~70px AI bar as 'the one section not counted' in the 980/988px budget, with the main window's scrollbar left on specifically as a fallback for that overflow case. Because the gate was always true, that fallback was silently engaged for 100% of users, not just the minority with an API key set — this fix makes the no-scrollbar case (no AI key, the default) actually achievable again, and confines the documented AI-bar-overflow tradeoff to only the sessions that opted into it.

New verification capability this session: got dearpygui actually rendering under this container's Xvfb (segfaulted at first — fixed with LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 and an explicit `-screen 0 1920x1080x24` xvfb-run arg) and captured real screenshots via dpg.output_frame_buffer() from a frame callback (must be called after a few rendered frames, not immediately after show_viewport — 'Render loop must have been started'). This is a genuine step up from every prior session's 'can't verify pixel-exact without a real display' caveat. Verified with actual screenshots, on a scratch copy of the repo (never the real studio_data/*.json): (1) with no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, no AI bar and no 'ai' header button, main window fits with no visible scrollbar; (2) with a fake ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set, both appear and the bar fits without visible clipping; (3) spot-checked the manual, MIDI mapping, and attribute-pools popups opened individually — all render cleanly with correct sizing, no clipped content.

Process note for future sessions: this screenshot technique (copy repo to scratch dir, monkeypatch dpg.start_dearpygui with a frame-counted callback that calls dpg.output_frame_buffer() then dpg.stop_dearpygui(), run under `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1920x1080x24"`) works in this container and should be reached for instead of static code reading whenever a change might affect layout — it would have caught this bug immediately.

Also noticed while auditing the changelog for context: the most recent commit before this session (2773932, 'add OSC target management GUI popup and persist targets to disk') has no corresponding changelog entry — a gap in a prior session's own record-keeping, left as-is here since it's not this session's change to document after the fact.
No schema or data changes; backward compatible. Scope: two one-line conditional fixes plus the layout-budget comment update explaining why.

entries.summary: Manual popup: documented the AI control surface + two missing header buttons
details: Re-audited the full roadmap list from scratch before touching anything: GUI polish (scroll fallback in place), manual/glossary popup, changelog popup, executor FLASH wired to real MIDI note-on/off, Block 12 AI layer (Anthropic client + action schema + execute()), MIDI mapping GUI (learn/reassign/delete), and attribute pool GUI panels were all already implemented and working — confirmed by reading the code paths directly, not just trusting prior changelog entries. No functional gap found there.

Found a real but purely-documentation gap instead: the '?' command manual had zero mention of the AI control surface — the ai prompt input box, the 10 built-in one-click chip prompts, the 'ai' header button (opens a save/run/delete prompt-pool popup, persisted to ai_prompts.json), the 'history' button (recent prompts + fired actions), and the token-usage readout. All of this has existed and worked for several sessions but a first-time user opening the manual would never discover it. Also missing: the 'mon' header button (programmer/output monitor popup with per-fixture RGB/dim/FX tables) wasn't listed in the KEYBOARD section's button rundown alongside MIDI/PATCH/PAGES/attr.

Added a new 'AI CONTROL' section to the manual (six rows: prompt box, chips, ai button, history button, token readout, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY requirement) and added 'mon button' / 'ai button' / 'log button' rows to the existing KEYBOARD section so every header button is now documented in one place.

Pure text addition inside _build_keys_popup's static _S list — no data model, schema, or behavior changes, so no backward-compatibility concerns. Verified with python3 -m py_compile and STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 (8/8 smoke test); confirmed via git status that studio_data/*.json was untouched by the run.

GUI sizing/clipping polish is still genuinely unverified from this container: dearpygui segfaults on import here even under xvfb-run (tried both bare and via Xvfb), so pixel-level layout checks remain out of reach — same limitation prior sessions hit, just confirmed again with a different failure mode (segfault instead of 'no display').

entries.summary: Cleanup: removed two dead/shadowed OutputState class definitions (~120 lines)
details: pyflakes flagged 'redefinition of unused OutputState' three times — the class was defined once in Block 7 (cue_layer/programmer_layer only, no FX), redefined in Block 8 (added fx_layer, additive-only FX), and redefined again after Block 9 (the real, currently-used version: LTP executor merge, audio_layer, master_level, blind, FX-replaces-base priority model). Only the last definition was ever reachable — output_state = OutputState(patch) at module bottom always bound to the final class. The first two were 100% dead code, never instantiated, and risked misleading future reads (including AI-assisted ones) about how output merging actually works.

Deleted the two superseded definitions, restored a docstring on the surviving class describing the real (four-layer + LTP) merge order, and removed a redundant 'import json' / 'import os' inside the Block 12 AI Engine section that shadowed the top-of-file imports for no reason.

Roadmap review: re-checked the file against the established roadmap list. Manual/glossary popup, changelog popup, MIDI mapping GUI (learn/reassign/delete), executor FLASH wired to real MIDI note-on/note-off (not just commands), and attribute pools (position/gobo/zoom/focus/beam — all have pool classes + GUI + persistence, just 0 presets recorded so far since the rig is RGB-only pixel tubes with no moving-light attributes) all turned out to already be implemented in prior sessions — no code changes needed there.

GUI sizing/clipping polish remains genuinely unverified: this environment can only run STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 (no display), so whether the 1920x1040 layout still clips on a real screen can't be checked from here. Left as-is per the hard rule against any other verification method — needs a human with a real display to confirm.

Environment note: this session's container had none of the project's dependencies installed (sacn, mido, python-rtmidi, python-osc, sounddevice, numpy, anthropic, dearpygui, plus the libportaudio2 system library) — had to pip/apt install all of them before the smoke test would even import. Not a code issue, just flagging in case future automated sessions hit the same cold-start.

entries.summary: FX engine: block/random/reverse/bounce distribution + pixel vs fixture scope
details: FX commands now accept BLOCK n, ORDER RANDOM, DIRECTION FWD|REV|BOUNCE, and PIXEL|FIXTURE.
target_scope lets any channel (not just dim) chase per-whole-fixture or per-individual-pixel across multiple tubes.
Dim FX can now drive individual pixels independently, not just whole fixtures.
Merged duplicated FX-bucketing logic (cue playback + programmer preview) into one shared _bucket_fx_defs().
All new params default to the exact old behavior (block_size=1, order=linear, direction=forward) — existing saved shows are unaffected.
FXPreset/fx_pool.json and cuestacks.json updated to persist the new fields.

entries.summary: MIDI startup no longer crashes when the controller isn't connected
details: MIDIEngine.start() now catches bad port index / port-open failures and continues without MIDI instead of raising.

entries.summary: Added STUDIO_DRY_RUN / STUDIO_HEADLESS environment switches
details: STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 runs the full FX/cue/output pipeline without opening a real sACN socket — nothing is sent to the fixtures.
STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 skips the GUI window and runs a scripted smoke test instead, for unattended/automated testing.
Smoke test exercises the FX -> RECORD CUE -> GO -> verify-FX-fires path this file's own doc comments had flagged as written but untested.

entries.summary: Fixed: headless test runs were writing into the real show files
details: First smoke-test run recorded a real 'Cue 5.0 Off' into the actual Cuestack 1 and cleared a pending 'FX FORM 8' the user had queued interactively — caught by diffing against the auto-generated .bak files and restored from them.
STUDIO_HEADLESS now redirects DATA_DIR to a fresh temp folder before any file is loaded, so RECORD/GO/save_show during automated runs can never touch studio_data/*.json.
STUDIO_DRY_RUN alone (GUI still open, manual use) intentionally still loads the real show — isolation only applies to unattended STUDIO_HEADLESS runs.

entries.summary: Executors: pages for organizing slots + flash (hold) trigger mode
details: PAGE <n> NAME <name>, PAGE <n> ADD|REMOVE EXEC <m>, PAGE LIST — purely organizational grouping of executor slots, doesn't affect playback. Persisted to executor_pages.json.
EXEC <n> MODE TOGGLE|FLASH sets how an executor is meant to be triggered (informational for now — GUI/MIDI wiring to actually use this comes in the GUI pass).

EXEC <n> FLASH ON|OFF fires a cue instantly (0s crossfade, reusing the existing per-executor time-override mechanism) and releases it fully on OFF — usable independent of trigger_mode, e.g. from a MIDI note's on/off callbacks the same way the existing 'Flash White' pad mapping already works.
Both verified via the STUDIO_HEADLESS smoke test (now 8/8 checks) plus a real dry-run: FLASH ON produced a 0.0s override crossfade vs. the cue's normal 2.0s.

entries.summary: GUI: manual popup extended, new changelog popup, MIDI flash-learn, partial sizing fix
details: The existing '?' button popup already was a sectioned command reference (manual/glossary) — extended it with the new FX distribution commands and EXEC/PAGE commands instead of building a duplicate.
Added a separate 'log' button/popup reading this changelog.json live and showing newest-first, per the user's request for two distinct popups.

Wired executor flash into MIDI: a new 'flash an executor while a pad is held' section in the MIDI popup lets you learn a note for EXEC <n> FLASH ON/OFF as a real on/off pad mapping, reusing the existing off_callback-capable MIDI-learn path. Dynamic targets ('Exec N Flash') regenerate correctly on restart, same pattern as the existing 'GO CS N CUE M' dynamic targets.

PARTIAL FIX, flagged for user verification: viewport was hardcoded 1920x1080 non-resizable at (0,0) — on this machine's actual 1920x1080 display, macOS's menu bar alone would push the bottom of that off-screen. Made viewport resizable, trimmed default height to 1040, and (more importantly) enabled scrolling on the main window and the manual popup, both of which had no_scrollbar=True — meaning any content overflow was being silently clipped with no way to reach it. Could not visually verify the actual rendered result (no display/screenshot access in this environment) — asked the user to confirm what's still cut off, if anything.

entries.summary: FX tree references: COLOR, GROUP, DIMREF
details: FX COLOR n drives all three RGB channels from ColorPreset n. Waveform controls pulse intensity toward that color.
FX SINE RED GROUP n targets only fixtures in GroupPool slot n instead of the programmer selection. Works on FIRE FX too: FIRE FX 3 GROUP 2.
FX SINE RED DIMREF n sets a live amplitude ceiling from DimmerPreset n. Change the preset level and the FX responds immediately with no re-fire.
RECORD FX saves color_id, dim_id, and group_id into the pool preset so references survive save/load.
_expand_color_fx and _expand_group_fx helpers resolve references before _bucket_fx_defs, keeping all existing behavior unchanged.
dim_pool wired into FXEngine and ExecutorPool so the DIMREF ceiling is available everywhere.

entries.summary: Command reference + cue button tooltips
details: Keyboard shortcut popup updated: FX COLOR, GROUP, DIMREF, FIRE FX GROUP, FX LIST, CLONE, OSC commands all documented.
Cue pool buttons now show a tooltip with cue name, fade time, and delay time on hover.

entries.summary: Active playbacks: FLASH hold button + cue timing editor
details: Each active executor row in the playbacks panel now has a 'flash' button. Hold it to fire EXEC n FLASH ON; release fires EXEC n FLASH OFF — detected via dpg.is_item_active() polling each tick, so it behaves as press-and-hold without requiring a separate release callback.

New 'cue timing' section in left column: two drag_float sliders (Fade s / Dly s) for the currently active cue. Dragging updates the cue in real time via CUE n FADE x and CUE n DELAY y commands. Sliders sync to the active cue on each tick but freeze while the user is dragging.

entries.summary: Executor fader level control + group pool fixture count tooltip
details: Each active executor row in the playbacks panel now has a full-width level slider (0–1 range) below the buttons. Dragging sets ex.level live; value persists to show file. EXEC n LEVEL 0–100 command also sets it from command line.
_H_MAIN expanded from 420 to 500 px so the left column has room for timing editor + fader rows without clipping.
Group pool buttons now show a tooltip with group name and fixture count on hover. Count is live (reads from patch each tick via Group.recall).

entries.summary: AI context enriched: programmer state, active executors, command history, token display
details: AI _state() now includes programmer contents, active executor states (cue, level, priority), and last 12 typed commands as context.
push_cmd_history() is called after every command-line entry, feeding recent console activity into future AI prompts.
New AI actions: group_select (select group by number), fx_stop (per-channel), exec_level (set executor fader), cue_fire (alias for goto_cue).
Token usage (input + output tokens) is displayed in the AI bar after each call. Token callback is installed once from the GUI on first send.

entries.summary: GUI error display + FX pool tree reference persistence
details: Command log now prefixes error responses with '⚠ ' — detected by matching Usage:/Error:/bad /not found/etc. prefixes from run_command results.
_log_error() added as the error-path log call; auto-detected in _on_cmd_execute by scanning the first line of each result string.

FX pool save (save_fx_pool) now writes dim_id, color_id, group_id for each layer. load_fx_pool passes them through add_layer on load. FXPreset.fire() passes color_id to fx_engine.add(). All three tree references now survive a save/load cycle.

entries.summary: Visual polish: SF Mono font + GO button amber theme
details: _load_console_font() loads /System/Library/Fonts/SFNSMono.ttf at 13px if available. Falls back silently to DearPyGui default if not found.
_make_go_theme() creates a distinct amber/orange button theme for the GO ▶ button — visually separated from other purple buttons so it reads as the primary action.
Both applied at build() time: font via dpg.bind_font(), GO theme via dpg.bind_item_theme('go_btn').

entries.summary: Attribute pool GUI panels: position, gobo, zoom, focus, beam

Each panel shows 12 slots (2 rows × 6 cols, compact 68px height) with name labels and hover tooltips.
Clicking a filled slot fires the corresponding POSITION/GOBO/ZOOM/FOCUS/BEAM command; empty slots log a record hint.
_attr_pools dict extracted as a module-level var and passed to GUIEngine via attr_pools= kwarg.
_tick_pools updates all 5 pools' button labels and tooltips each tick.

entries.summary: Visual polish continued: BACK button blue theme + cue list fade times
details: _make_back_theme() adds a distinct muted blue to the BACK ◀ button — GO is amber, BACK is blue, all other buttons remain default purple.
Cue list in the left column now shows fade time inline after the cue name (e.g. '[3]  Intro  2.0s') so timing is visible without hovering.

entries.summary: FX editor gets group/color/dim reference dropdowns + theme and v0.15
details: Each layer row in the FX preset editor now shows three compact combo boxes (Grp / Col / Dim) for assigning live GroupPool, ColorPool, and DimPool references. Saved through preset.add_layer() and persist to fx_pool.json.

Version bumped to v0.15.

entries.summary: FX LIST now shows active executor FX + executor assignments persist across restarts
details: FX LIST command output now includes an 'Active executor FX' section listing each running executor's FX layers (waveform, channel, BPM, size). Previously only programmer FX and pool contents were shown.

Executor→cuestack assignments, level, priority, and trigger_mode now saved to studio_data/executors.json on every SAVE. Loaded at startup so GO works immediately after restart without re-running ASSIGN CS <n> TO EXEC <n>.

entries.summary: Theme: violet accent, colored pool buttons, cuestack combo, keyboard shortcuts
details: Accent color changed from warm peach to violet #8b5cf6 (139,92,246) per original design spec. GO button remains amber, BACK remains blue.
Color pool buttons now show the preset's actual color as a background tint (dark resting / mid hover / full-bright active). Empty slots revert to default.
Dim pool buttons now show a brightness-scaled blue tint and a tooltip with the preset name and level %.
Left-column cuestack title replaced by a clickable combo — select any cuestack from the dropdown to switch the active cue list instantly.
Keyboard shortcuts added: Cmd/Ctrl+S saves the show; F5 fires GO; F4 fires BACK. Ctrl/Cmd+letter combos no longer accidentally append to the command input.

entries.summary: MIDI startup hardened against missing MIDI backend entirely (not just missing device)
details: Found while re-verifying the headless smoke test in a fresh container: MIDIEngine.list_ports() and start() both called mido.get_input_names() unguarded. That call raises an rtmidi-internal exception (not OSError/IOError, so the existing 'no port found' handling didn't catch it) when there's no ALSA/CoreMIDI backend available at all — e.g. a container with no /dev/snd/seq — as opposed to a backend that's present but has zero devices plugged in. Previously this crashed the whole app at import time, before the GUI or dry-run pipeline ever started.
Both call sites now catch broadly and print a 'MIDI backend unavailable' message, continuing without MIDI — same fallback behavior as the existing 'no device plugged in' and 'bad port index' cases.
STUDIO_DRY_RUN=1 STUDIO_HEADLESS=1 smoke test: 8/8 passing after the fix.

Note for the user, not a decision that needs one: this session also attempted the same 'Attribute pool GUI panels' roadmap item and found another session had already landed it (commits 887b10f/de4f3e9) with a different design — 5 always-visible panel rows in the main pools section rather than a popup. Discarded the duplicate rather than merge two designs. Flagging a real but unverified risk in that landed design: rows 4-5 add roughly two more 78px panel rows (~160px) to the main window's stacked content, on top of a layout that a prior session already flagged as tight for 1920x1080 (see the 'partial sizing fix' entry above, also unverified for the same reason — no display/screenshot access in this environment). The main window already has scrolling enabled as a fallback so this shouldn't crash or clip unreachably, but it likely means a visible scrollbar now where the roadmap goal was none. Worth a visual check next time the console runs on a real screen.

entries.summary: Visual polish: RGB-tinted bars, tap tempo, fade progress, BLIND/BLACKOUT, new commands
details: Output monitor and programmer monitor progress bars now tint to the fixture's actual RGB color — a red fixture shows a red bar, blue shows blue. Themes are cached and only rebuilt when the color changes.
Tap tempo button added to the FX section label row. Click it repeatedly to set BPM from tap intervals (auto-resets after 3s gap). Rate BPM slider and all live FX layers update immediately.

Each active executor row in the playbacks panel now shows a 4px amber fade progress bar below the level fader. Fills from 0→100% during a crossfade with overlay text showing percentage and total seconds. FadeEngine.fade_progress() added to expose this without touching internal state.

BLIND command suppresses the programmer layer from DMX output while keeping it visible in the monitors and stage preview — safe editing without affecting the live output. LIVE restores it. Red status bar indicator shows when active.

BLACKOUT command cuts master_level to 0.0 instantly, saving the pre-blackout level for restore. BLACKOUT OFF or a second BLACKOUT restores. BBO is a one-key alias. Red '■ BBO' status bar indicator. Master fader in stage panel syncs to 0.
SNAPSHOT <n> [name] records the full current live look (cue + programmer merged, across all running executors) as a standalone cue. Unlike RECORD CUE which only records programmer content.
DELETE CUE <n> [CS <m>] removes a cue from a cuestack and saves the show. The underlying CueStack.delete_cue() method already existed but was never exposed via command parser.
CUE <n> SHOW prints a summary of what's stored in a specific cue: fade/delay times, per-fixture dim and FX defs, and a compact per-color count of sub-fixture pixel values.
GOTO and ASSIGN CS <n> TO EXEC <n> documented in command reference. Keyboard shortcut reference updated with F5/F4/Cmd+S and tap tempo. RENAME/COPY section renamed RENAME/COPY/DELETE.

entries.summary: Fix OSC fader/key handlers silently dropping every executor except Page 1 Exec 1
details: Re-audited the established roadmap first (GUI polish, manual popup, changelog popup, MIDI-held FLASH, Block 12 AI layer, MIDI mapping GUI, attribute pool panels) -- all confirmed already landed by prior sessions via direct code inspection, not just trusting the changelog. Ran a background research pass over the whole file (dead code, manual-vs-parser mismatches, MIDI/OSC symmetry, attribute pool CRUD parity) looking for the next real gap rather than re-doing finished work.

Found one: _osc_fader and _osc_key (the /gma3/fader/PAGE/EXEC and /gma3/key/PAGE/EXEC/TYPE MA3-style OSC input handlers) parsed page and exec_num out of the incoming OSC address correctly, but then gated all actual behavior on 'if page == 1 and exec_num == 1' -- a placeholder from when the console only had one executor wired up ('We map Page 1 Exec 1 -> grandmaster dim for now'). Every other executor was parsed, logged to console, and silently dropped, despite the console fully supporting many executors via the existing EXEC <n> GO/BACK/LEVEL command family that MIDI targets already use freely.

_osc_fader now keeps the legacy Page 1 Exec 1 -> grandmaster-dim mapping (so existing OSC templates don't change behavior) but routes any other page/exec straight to that executor's own .level field -- the same field the GUI executor sliders write via _on_exec_fader, and written directly (no save_show() call) so a fast fader sweep doesn't hammer disk I/O on every OSC message, matching how the GUI slider already behaves.

_osc_key keeps Page 1 Exec 1 Go/Back mapped to the active executor (cue_go()/cue_back(), unchanged) but routes any other page/exec through run_command('EXEC <n> GO') or 'EXEC <n> BACK' -- the identical command path the text command line and MIDI note targets use, so a TouchOSC/Chataigne page can now drive any executor, not just the first one.

This console does not have grandMA3-style paging of executor numbers (PAGE here organizes cuestacks for display only, per ExecutorPool.pages -- confirmed while investigating, does not affect playback), so 'page' in the OSC address is accepted for compatibility with MA3-shaped OSC templates but otherwise ignored; exec_num alone selects the executor.
